observations.empty_band: 4E88, between the message body text and the 出所 line — measured directly on the pixels, A15D has ~14px of blank space there while 4E88 has ~56px, about 4x larger, with nothing (no divider, no extra element) explaining it. The gap from 出所 to the button row is ~20px in both, so the anomaly is isolated to this one spot in 4E88.
observations.content_lost: neither — checked item by item: '# Slack' header, title 'このメッセージを送りますか？', '↗ 外部に出る' link, 宛先 #sales, 差出人 あなた, the body sentence, the 出所 line '週次同期・田中・10:42 >', and the Cancel/Edit/送る buttons are all present and textually identical in both images.

why.visual_craft: 4E88's ~56px unexplained gap before 出所 reads as a layout defect rather than a deliberate choice; A15D's tighter, even spacing looks intentional.
why.spacing_rhythm: A15D keeps a consistent short-gap/longer-gap rhythm (14px then 20px); 4E88 breaks that rhythm with a 56px gap in the first slot while the second slot stays ~21px, so the two gaps no longer relate to each other proportionally.
why.information_hierarchy: Proximity ties the 出所 line to the message it describes; A15D's 14px gap preserves that grouping while 4E88's 56px gap visually orphans 出所 from the body it annotates.
why.preview_readability: Same text and type size in both, but 4E88 forces a longer visual jump from the end of the message to its source line, interrupting the reading flow that A15D keeps tight.
why.provenance_visibility: The source text itself is identical in size/contrast, but A15D's closer placement makes its association with the message clearer; 4E88's isolation reads as accidental rather than an intentional emphasis.
why.control_reachability: The gap before the button row is ~20px in A15D and ~21px in 4E88 — effectively the same — so button placement and reachability do not differ meaningfully.
why.overall: A15D delivers the same content with tighter, coherent spacing; 4E88 has an unexplained ~56px gap between the body and the 出所 line that looks like a mistake, which is the deciding factor.
